items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Lloyd and Linda Van Wyck, Kitchener
notes:
Lloyd Van Wyck encouraged the Region to adopt a discounted fare for senior citizens using Grand River Transit (GRT), noting that other municipalities have lower fares for seniors and that requiring seniors to prove need is insulting. He stated that a fare reduction may increase ridership and thus increase revenue, and requested that it be adopted as a pilot project.

Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation Services, explained that GRT has moved away from discounts based on age to discounts based on need, being the affordable transit program. He noted that staff have looked at senior’s fares as a part of the GRT business plan which will be presented in April, and that the plan will be shared with the delegation.

items.title: Swami Chaitanya Jyoti, Head Priest
notes:
Vikas Tomar spoke on behalf of the Shri Ram Dham Hindu Temple. He noted that currently the Temple is not accessible by GRT and they are requesting that GRT service be made available. He provided an overview of the services and activities available at the Temple, including counseling to newcomers and intergenerational programs. He stressed that GRT service would allow seniors that don’t have vehicles to access the space.

In response to a question from Council, D. Spooner noted that he has spoken with representatives from the Temple about transit demand. He explained that staff have looked at the possibility of bringing a bus stop closer and running the service on Saturdays and Sundays, which would cost $720,000 on an annual basis and is not included in 2025 service plan. Council requested that staff bring options for including pilot days and the financial implications in the April cycle.

items.title: Susanna Compton, Waterloo
notes: S. Compton appeared in support of farmers and in opposition to the Wilmot land assembly noting that farmland is needed to ensure access to made in Canada products. She noted that the countryside line was the hard line that allowed farmers to confidently invest in their farms and the land assembly cuts in to that. She stated that the farmland in Waterloo Region is the highest quality in Canada and able to grow more diverse food options than anywhere in North America, except California. She encouraged the Region to stop the land assembly and fight for reinstating the countryside line.

items.title: John-Lee Bannister, Waterloo
notes: J. Bannister, First Vice President of the Waterloo Labour Council, spoke in favour of CUPE 1656 and the importance of the work that the members do. He encouraged the Region to give the workers everything that they have asked for. J. Bannister further highlighted the renewed bombing in Palestine and encouraged everyone to get involved with Palestinian support agencies in the community.

items.title: Board of Health Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang Commissioner, Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health, noted that there has been increased measles activity in Southern Ontario including in the neighbouring public health unit and areas of concern in neighbouring areas. She highlighted that no cases have been found in Waterloo Region, and encouraged the public to ensure they are up to date on their vaccinations and monitor their family and self for any symptoms especially after travel internationally or to areas where there are high cases. Dr. H. Wang spoke to school vaccinations noting that 6500 student records are not up to date, and explained how parents can avoid suspensions, which will begin on April 2, 2025.

Responding to questions, Dr. H. Wang explained that the required vaccinations for measles depends on the individual and people should talk to a medical provider with access to their personal history. She further noted that the only treatment for measles is to treat the symptoms and the best action is to avoid getting it.

In response to a question from Council regarding the length of school suspensions, Dr. H. Wang stated that the Act provides for up to a twenty-day suspension, unless the student is immunized or their record updated.

Council recessed at 7:45 p.m. and reconvened at 7:58 p.m.

items.title: PDL-CAS-25-006, Municipal Diversity Plan – Waterloo Regional Police Services Board (2025)
notes:
William Short, Regional Clerk, provided an overview of the plan. He stressed that the Community Safety and Policing Act requires that this plan be in place by April 1, 2025 but that consultation work will be done to refine the plan before the next public appointment to the police board after the 2026 municipal election.

C. Huinink requested that accessibility be incorporated into the plan and that the acronym be changed to READI rather than REDI.

In response to a question from Council, W. Short explained that should the Police Services Board be expanded to nine members, the legislation requires that the additional members be an Provincial appointee and a Regional Councillor.

Council recognized the importance of advocating to the province for ensuring that they recognize the importance of diversity with their appointments.

motions.item_title: Community and Health Services Committee Summary - March 4, 2025
motions.text: The Community and Health Services Committee recommends as follows: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the revised Building Better Futures Framework set out in Appendix A, as the Region of Waterloo’s direction for the continued creation and protection of affordable and non-market housing over the next five years (2025 to 2030), contingent upon federal and provincial funding, as outlined in report CSD-HOU-25-003, dated March 4, 2025. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions with regard to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation Affordable Housing Funding (CMHC AHF) for 589 Langs Drive, Cambridge as outlined in report CSD-HOU-25-002 dated March 4, 2025: Authorize the Regional Municipality of Waterloo to enter into a loan agreement with Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation for the construction of the Waterloo Region Housing (WRH) affordable housing building 589 Langs Dr., Cambridge; Authorize the Commissioner of Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer to execute the loan agreement with CMHC and all ancillary documentation in a form satisfactory to both the Chief Financial Officer and the Regional Solicitor; and Authorize the Director, Housing Services, to execute and deliver all other administrative documentation as required by CMHC after substantial completion to fulfill requirements.

  • Maintain the current composition of the Board at seven members;
  • Staff will return prior to the 2026 appointment of the Waterloo Regional Police Services Board with a review and update of the Municipal Diversity Plan to outline public engagement strategies, and update of application process; and
  • That the Regional Chair write a letter to the province to advocate for the recommended knowledge and experience for provincial representatives who are appointed to the Waterloo Regional Police Services Board;

as outlined in report PDL-CAS-25-006, dated March 19, 2025.
